events.text: world_loader.zig is co-edited (req_0524 streaming lane, uncommitted) — my spawn/collider fix is verified in the shared working tree (headless run: grounded=true on a city floor plate, /tmp/spawn-probe.png); deferring the git commit until that lane lands to avoid sweeping foreign hunks

resolution: Root-caused with loader probes run against the user's real baked map. THREE stacked failures: (1) chooseSpawn picked the nearest FLAT instance to the all-instance centre — a 61×1m road paint stripe in the void (no width filter, and the wanted centre wasn't the city); (2) the near-field collider window (±3 cells × 64m over a 14,877-piece city) emits more floors than MAX_RECTS=4096 and scanned cells in raw lo→hi order, so even the player's OWN cell lost the cap race — probes showed underCol=0: literally zero rects under the player, a guaranteed fall regardless of spawn height; (3) scene.heightfields=0 in this bake, so the earlier terrain clamp had nothing to clamp to. Fixes (working tree, verified headless: player grounded=true on an authored floor plate at the city, screenshot /tmp/spawn-probe.png): rebuildWindow now emits rings 0-1 around the player FIRST, then the spanning list, then outer rings — the cap only ever drops the far field; chooseSpawn aims at the authored-piece bbox centre, scans ALL rows including piece plates, and requires a real >=2x2m floor (a stripe can't be the spawn floor); boot-time spawn/spawn-column probes + screenshot-gated per-frame ground probes stay in for the next hunt. COMMIT DEFERRED: world_loader.zig is co-edited by the req_0524 streaming lane (uncommitted foreign hunks); the fix rides the shared tree now and commits when that lane lands.
